title: fix(app-shell,data-objectstack): concurrent identical Studio reads share one in-flight request (objectui#11797)
body:
Fixes #11797

Clause-②: no

## What changes

Opening a Studio package mounts several readers that ask the same question at once, and each one sent its own request. A caller that arrives while an identical request is still pending now waits for that request instead of sending another:

- **`fetchPackages`** (`@object-ui/app-shell`, `studio-design/packages-io.ts`): the package switcher, the writability courtesy gate and the `DataPillar` namespace lookup share one `GET /api/v1/packages`.
- **`fetchPendingDrafts`** (`@object-ui/app-shell`, `preview/usePendingDrafts.ts`): the hook's mount read and the surface's own mount `refresh()` (Studio top bar, chat bar) share one `GET /api/v1/meta/_drafts` per scope.
- **`MetadataClient`** (`@object-ui/data-objectstack`, `metadata-client.ts`): `listTypes`, `list`, `listDrafts` and `get` / `getDraft` share one GET per method, URL and headers. The sharing works across every client built on the same `fetch`, because the console creates one client per component, all on one authenticated fetch. Every caller, the first one included, gets an answer object no other caller holds: the last caller to be handed the answer takes the parsed original and every earlier one a `structuredClone` copy, so nothing is copied when nobody joined (patch round 1, `bab3004`).

No call site changed. The `fetchPackages` call sites in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and `BuilderLanding.tsx` are untouched: the read is shared below them.

## Measured: the duplicates are concurrent mounts, and in-flight sharing alone removes them (H1)

Requests are counted on the wire, through transports that hold every request open until the test answers it. **Before** is the ablation run: the three production files checked out at the base `455c646`, with the tests unchanged.

| What | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| The real `StudioDesignSurface` on the Data tab: `GET /api/v1/packages` | 3 | 1 |
| The same render: `_drafts?packageId=…` | not reached (the packages assertion fails first) | 1 |
| Two count surfaces (the hook plus their own mount refresh) on one package: `_drafts` | 4 | 1 |
| Two `MetadataClient`s on one fetch, each calling `listDrafts`, `list` and `get` | 6 | 3 |
| Three concurrent `fetchPackages()` calls | 3 | 1 |

The before counts match the card's "packages ×3" and "_drafts ×4" readings.

## Design: in-flight sharing only, with no reuse window (H2)

I cannot name every write that must clear a cached answer. An agent creates packages and stages drafts on the server, and the client never sees those writes. So, per H2, this keeps **only** the in-flight sharing, with no reuse window:

- An entry is dropped the moment its request settles, so a call made after an answer always goes to the server.
- A read already on the wire when a write lands was asked before that write, so a read asked after the write must not join it. The writes each reader can see drop the pending entry:
  - **`MetadataClient`:** every `save`, `publishDraft`, `publishPackageDrafts`, `reset`, `publish` and `rollback` through a client on the same `fetch` drops every pending read on that `fetch`. The drop happens when the write's response arrives, whether the write succeeded or failed.
  - **packages:** `duplicatePackage` (the same module) and the existing `objectui:packages-changed` announcement (create and edit, from `PackageFormDialog`).
  - **drafts:** the publish pulse (`emitMetadataRefresh`), which the module doc already names as the contract every publish path keeps. The drop runs before the hooks it wakes read again, so those hooks share **one** new request.
- **Residual:** a write the reader cannot see (a package delete or disable through `PackagesPage`, a draft save while a raw `_drafts` read is pending, any server-side agent write) can still be answered by a read that was already on the wire. The window is one round trip, and the same residual applies to the adapter's existing `find` sharing. A read asked after that pending read settles always goes to the server.

Failures are shared, not remembered (H3). A failed request rejects every caller that was waiting on it, and the next call retries. Tests cover an HTTP failure and a transport failure (`fetch` rejecting) for the metadata client.

No exported signature changes (H4). There is no new export, method, option or type. `shareRead`, `sendWrite`, `readPackagesPayload` and `readDraftsPayload` are all module-private or `private`.

## `sys_user_preference`: no duplicate to remove (the premise does not hold for this family)

The card reported three `GET /api/v1/data/sys_user_preference` reads "with the identical filter" on Home → Studio. I measured this through the real `ObjectStackAdapter` and client (`userState.inflightShare-11797.test.ts`). `UserStateBridge` attaches three adapters, one each for `ui.favorites`, `ui.recent` and `ui.flow.palette.recents`, and each one loads its own row. The result is three requests whose filters differ only in the `key` predicate, which sits at the tail of a long encoded query string. They are three different questions, so one read per key is already met. The real duplicate case is two loads of one `(user, key)` at once, and the adapter's existing `find` sharing already sends that as one request (pinned). **`userState.ts` is not changed.**

## Files

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/packages-io.ts`
- `packages/app-shell/src/preview/usePendingDrafts.ts`
- `packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts`
- `packages/data-objectstack/README.md`: the **Shared In-Flight Reads** bullet now covers `MetadataClient` (patch round 1)
- Tests: `packages-io.inflightShare-11797.test.tsx`, `StudioDesignSurface.entryReadsOnce-11797.test.tsx` (a new test file beside `packages-io.ts`; `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` itself is not edited), `usePendingDrafts.inflightShare-11797.test.tsx`, `metadata-client.inflightShare-11797.test.ts`, `userState.inflightShare-11797.test.ts`
- `.changeset/11797-shared-inflight-reads.md`: patch for `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/data-objectstack`

## Verification

Round 0 ran at `c3759d6`. Patch round 1 re-ran at `bab3004` (the final commit): new pins, 5 files / 32 tests passed; regression, the same 247-file set, 247 files / 2233 tests passed; app-shell and data-objectstack type-check exit 0. The figures below are round 0's.

- **New pins** (5 files, run with `pnpm exec vitest run` from the repo root): `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 27 passed (27)`.
- **Ablation:**
  - Each production file was checked out at `455c646`, and on-disk markers confirmed the swap: the hash equals the BASE blob for all 3 files.
  - Result: `Test Files 4 failed | 1 passed (5)`, `Tests 12 failed | 15 passed (27)`. The `sys_user_preference` file stays green because it pins existing behaviour.
  - Restored with `git checkout HEAD --`: the hash equals the HEAD blob for all 3 files, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. After the restore: `Test Files 5 passed (5)`.
- **Regression:**
  - Scope: every test file that imports a touched module or builds a `MetadataClient`, plus all of `packages/data-objectstack/` and `StudioRoute`. That is 247 files across app-shell, data-objectstack, plugin-designer, plugin-form, plugin-kanban, plugin-calendar, react and console.
  - Result: `Test Files 247 passed (247)`, `Tests 2228 passed (2228)`.
  - This is a declared narrowing. The full 8-shard `pnpm test` is left to CI.
- **Builds and type-checks:**
  - `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...`: exit 0.
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack type-check`: exit 0.
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`, which runs both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` (the second includes `src/**/*.test.ts(x)`): exit 0.
- **Lint:** `pnpm exec eslint` on the 8 touched source and test files: exit 0, with 0 errors and 9 warnings. All 9 warnings are on lines that were already there (`any` casts in `listTypes`, `setState` in the effect).
- **Repo gates:**
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: `✅ 8 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`.
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
  - `pnpm check:control-bytes`: `✅ check-control-bytes: OK`.
  - Also exit 0: `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:metadata-write-doors`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`, and `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (NOT GOVERNED).
- **NOT MEASURED:**
  - `check:published-dist`: it builds every package including the console app, which is a repo-wide run that CI owns. A local attempt was stopped by a 300 s timeout before it printed a verdict.
  - `check:dist-completeness --all` for app-shell: app-shell itself was not built locally (only its dependency closure was). The gate reported only that unbuilt package, and no other.

## Acceptance notes (not fixed here, not filed)

- **README gap, resolved in patch round 1** (`bab3004`, seat verdict `6050853625`). The data-objectstack README bullet "Shared In-Flight Reads" describes only the adapter's `find` and `findOne`. A sentence about `MetadataClient` sharing is owed under AGENTS.md #2, but the README is outside this card's claimed file surface, so I left it for the seat.
- **`find` is not dropped by writes.** `ObjectStackAdapter.emitMutation` drops the pending `findOne` reads of the resource it writes, but not the pending `find` reads. A list refetch asked after a write can therefore join a `find` that was sent before the write. This was found by reading the code, with no public-door reproduction.
- **A second packages reader.** `ContextSelectors` (the app top bar) reads its options endpoint with its own `fetch`, separately from `fetchPackages`. It is not part of the Studio entry path.
- **Not measured:** whether Home → Studio remounts `ConnectedShell` and so re-attaches the user-state bridge. That would explain why the three preference reads repeat on that navigation, but they are still one read per key.
- **Hung requests.** A request that never settles keeps its joiners waiting. This is the same property as the adapter's existing `find` / `findOne` sharing.
- **Overlap with objectui#11799.** That card is queued behind this one and touches the `?state=draft` probe. This PR changes only the transport under `readItemResponse` (now wrapped in `shareRead`); the probe logic is unchanged.

The implementing session is `https://claude.ai/code/session_01MgfduSkFrfM3eorB3UGfAU` (seat `domain:ui#2`).
